   581	): boolean {
   582	  const slot = option.activationChoice;
   583	  if (slot === undefined || slot === null) return choice === null || choice === undefined;
   584	  if (choice === null || choice === undefined || choice.kind !== slot.kind) return false;
   585	  switch (slot.kind) {
   586	    case 'command_word':
   587	      return choice.kind === 'command_word' && slot.values.some((value) => value === choice.value);
   588	    case 'unicorns_blessing_spell':
   589	      return choice.kind === 'unicorns_blessing_spell' && slot.values.some((value) => value === choice.value);
   590	    case 'dispel_evil_and_good_mode':
   591	      return choice.kind === 'dispel_evil_and_good_mode' && slot.values.some((value) => value === choice.value);
   592	    case 'calm_emotions_per_target': {
   593	      if (choice.kind !== 'calm_emotions_per_target') return false;
   594	      const expected = [...slot.targetIds].sort();
   595	      const actual = choice.selections.map((entry) => entry.targetId).sort();
   596	      return expected.length === actual.length && expected.every((value, index) => value === actual[index]) &&
   597	        new Set(actual).size === actual.length &&
   598	        choice.selections.every((entry) => slot.values.some((value) => value === entry.mode));
   599	    }
   600	  }
   601	}

   603	export function mechanicsWithChoice(
   604	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
   605	  choice: EngineActivationChoice | null | undefined,
   606	  option: EngineOfferableOption,
   607	): ResolvedTurnMechanics {
   608	  if (choice === null || choice === undefined) return mechanics;
   609	  const owningSpellIds = choice.kind === 'command_word'
   610	    ? ['command']
   611	    : choice.kind === 'unicorns_blessing_spell'
   612	      ? ['cure-wounds', 'lesser-restoration']
   613	      : choice.kind === 'dispel_evil_and_good_mode'
   614	        ? ['dispel-evil-and-good']
   615	        : ['calm-emotions'];
   616	  const owner = option.actionSlots.flatMap((slot) => slot.use.kind === 'cast_spell'
   617	    ? [{ slot: slot.slot, use: slot.use }]
   618	    : []).find((slot) => owningSpellIds.includes(slot.use.spellId) &&
   619	      (choice.kind !== 'unicorns_blessing_spell' || slot.slot === 'bonus'));
   620	  if (owner === undefined) return mechanics;
   621	  return {
   622	    ...mechanics,
   623	    actionSlots: mechanics.actionSlots.map((slot) => {
   624	      if (slot.kind !== 'cast_spell' || slot.slot !== owner.slot ||
   625	        slot.actionId !== owner.use.sourceActionId || slot.spellId !== owner.use.spellId) return slot;
   626	      return {
   627	        ...slot,
   628	        spellId: choice.kind === 'unicorns_blessing_spell' ? engineSpellId(choice.value) : slot.spellId,
   629	        activationChoice: choice,
   630	      };
   631	    }),
   632	  };
   633	}

   635	export function availableEngineActorOptions(
   636	  state: EncounterState,
   637	  actorId: CombatantId,
   638	  environment: EngineOptionEnvironment,
   639	  revision = state.revision,
   640	): readonly EngineOfferableOption[] {
   641	  return engineActorOptionsForEnvironment(state, actorId, environment, revision).offerable
   642	    .filter((option) => resolveEngineActorOption(state, option, environment).valid);
   643	}
   644	
   645	function accepted(
   646	  selectedBranch: 'primary' | 'fallback',
   647	  option: EngineOfferableOption,
   648	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
   649	  primaryOption: EngineOfferableOption,
   650	  fallbackOption: EngineOfferableOption | null,
   651	  refusals: Extract<EngineProposalResolution, { readonly valid: true }>['refusals'] = [],
   652	): EngineProposalResolution {
   653	  const resolutionDigest = sha256(canonicalJson(mechanics));
   654	  return {
   655	    valid: true,
   656	    selectedBranch,
   657	    resolutionDigest,
   658	    summary: `${mechanics.actorId} expands ${option.label} into ${String(mechanics.actionSlots.length)} ordered use(s) after ${String(mechanics.movementCostFeet)} feet`,
   659	    mechanics,
   660	    option,
   661	    primaryOption,
   662	    fallbackOption,
   663	    refusals,
   664	  };
   665	}

   667	export function createPureTurnProposalResolver(
   668	  environment: EngineOptionEnvironment,
   669	): PureTurnProposalResolver {
   670	  return Object.freeze({
   671	    resolve(state: EncounterState, proposal: EngineTurnProposal): EngineProposalResolution {
   672	      const options = availableEngineActorOptions(
   673	        state,
   674	        proposal.actorId,
   675	        environment,
   676	        proposal.expectedRevision,
   677	      );
   678	      const primary = options.find((option) => option.optionId === proposal.primaryOptionId);
   679	      if (primary !== undefined) {
   680	        const resolution = resolveEngineActorOption(state, primary, environment);
   681	        if (resolution.valid) {
   682	          const fallback = proposal.fallbackOptionId === null
   683	            ? null
   684	            : options.find((option) => option.optionId === proposal.fallbackOptionId) ?? null;
   685	          if (!choiceFitsOption(primary, proposal.activationChoice)) {
   686	            return { valid: false, selectedBranch: 'none', refusals: [{ branch: 'primary', code: 'ACTIVATION_CHOICE_INVALID', summary: `${proposal.actorId}: activation choice does not match the offered option` }] };
   687	          }
   688	          return accepted('primary', primary, mechanicsWithChoice(resolution.mechanics, proposal.activationChoice, primary), primary, fallback);
   689	        }
   690	      }
   691	      const primaryRefusal = {
   692	        branch: 'primary' as const,
   693	        code: 'OPTION_NOT_OFFERED',
   694	        summary: `${proposal.actorId}: primary option was not offered at revision ${String(proposal.expectedRevision)}`,
   695	      };
   696	      if (proposal.fallbackOptionId === null) return { valid: false, selectedBranch: 'none', refusals: [primaryRefusal] };
   697	      const fallback = options.find((option) => option.optionId === proposal.fallbackOptionId);
   698	      if (fallback === undefined) {
   699	        return {
   700	          valid: false,
   701	          selectedBranch: 'none',
   702	          refusals: [primaryRefusal, { branch: 'fallback', code: 'OPTION_NOT_OFFERED', summary: `${proposal.actorId}: fallback option was not offered at revision ${String(proposal.expectedRevision)}` }],
   703	        };
   704	      }
   705	      const resolution = resolveEngineActorOption(state, fallback, environment);
   706	      return resolution.valid
   707	        ? choiceFitsOption(fallback, proposal.activationChoice)
   708	          ? accepted('fallback', fallback, mechanicsWithChoice(resolution.mechanics, proposal.activationChoice, fallback), primary ?? fallback, fallback, [primaryRefusal])
   709	          : { valid: false, selectedBranch: 'none', refusals: [primaryRefusal, { branch: 'fallback', code: 'ACTIVATION_CHOICE_INVALID', summary: `${proposal.actorId}: activation choice does not match the fallback option` }] }
   710	        : { valid: false, selectedBranch: 'none', refusals: [primaryRefusal, { branch: 'fallback', code: resolution.code, summary: resolution.summary }] };
   711	    },
   712	  });
   713	}

    27	function declaredIdentity(optionValue: EngineOfferableOption): EngineDeclaredOptionIdentity {

    29	  if (primary === undefined || primary.kind !== 'disengage') {

    35	function humanOnlyOption(
    36	  revision: number,

    39	  declaredOption: EngineDeclaredOptionIdentity,
    40	  noModeledEffect: EngineHumanOnlyOption['noModeledEffect'],
    41	): EngineHumanOnlyOption {

    49	function unsupportedSpellCandidates(
    50	  state: EncounterState,
    51	  actorId: CombatantId,
    52	  revision: number,
    53	): readonly EngineHumanOnlyOption[] {
    54	  const subject = state.combatants.find((candidate) => candidate.profile.id === actorId);
    55	  const actions = [
    56	    ...declaredMonsterActions(state, actorId).map((action) => ({ action, slot: 'main' as const })),
    57	    ...declaredMonsterBonusActions(state, actorId).map((action) => ({ action, slot: 'bonus' as const })),
    58	  ];
    59	  return actions.flatMap(({ action, slot }) => {

    63	      const remaining = poolId === null

    66	      if (remaining !== null && remaining < 1) return [];

    80	                )
    81	                ? 'targeting_unresolved'
    82	                : null;

   101	          sourceActionId: engineActionId(action.id),
   102	          spellId: engineSpellId(spell.id),
   103	          slot,
   104	        },
   105	        modeling.reason,
   106	      )];
   107	    });
   108	  });
   109	}

   111	function unsupportedActionCandidates(
   112	  state: EncounterState,
   113	  actorId: CombatantId,
   114	  revision: number,
   115	): readonly EngineHumanOnlyOption[] {
   116	  return declaredMonsterActions(state, actorId).flatMap((action) => {

   120	      case 'multiattack': return [];

   122	      case 'spellcasting': break;

   125	    const actionId = engineActionId(declaredActionId);
   126	    const modeling = classifyOptionModeling(state, {
   127	      kind: 'unsupported_action',
   128	      actionId,
   129	      actionKind: action.kind,
   130	      sourceNote: action.execution.note,
   131	    });
   132	    if (modeling.kind === 'primary_effect_modeled') {
   133	      throw new RangeError('An unsupported action candidate cannot be offerable.');
   134	    }
   135	    return [humanOnlyOption(
   136	      revision,
   137	      actorId,
   138	      declaredActionId,
   139	      { kind: 'action', actionId, actionKind: action.kind },
   140	      modeling.reason,
   141	    )];
   142	  });
   143	}

   145	function unsupportedBonusActionCandidates(
   146	  state: EncounterState,

   148	  revision: number,

   150	  return declaredMonsterBonusActions(state, actorId).flatMap((action) => {
   151	    if (!('execution' in action) || action.execution.kind !== 'absent') return [];
   152	    const declaredActionId = 'id' in action ? action.id : `bonus:${action.kind}`;
   153	    const actionId = engineActionId(declaredActionId);
   154	    const modeling = classifyOptionModeling(state, {
   155	      kind: 'unsupported_action',
   156	      actionId,
   157	      actionKind: action.kind,
   158	      sourceNote: action.execution.note,
   159	    });
   160	    if (modeling.kind === 'primary_effect_modeled') {
   161	      throw new RangeError('An unsupported bonus-action candidate cannot be offerable.');
   162	    }
   163	    return [humanOnlyOption(
   164	      revision,
   165	      actorId,
   166	      declaredActionId,
   167	      { kind: 'action', actionId, actionKind: action.kind },
   168	      modeling.reason,
   169	    )];
   170	  });
   171	}

   173	export interface EngineActorOptionPartition {
   174	  readonly offerable: readonly EngineOfferableOption[];
   175	  readonly humanOnly: readonly EngineHumanOnlyOption[];
   176	  readonly candidates: readonly EngineOptionCandidate[];
   177	}
   178	
   179	export interface HiddenOptionRecord {
   180	  readonly actorId: CombatantId;
   181	  readonly humanOptionId: EngineHumanOptionId;
   182	  readonly declaredOption: EngineDeclaredOptionIdentity;
   183	  readonly reason: EngineHumanOnlyOption['noModeledEffect'];
   184	}
   185	
   186	export function engineActorOptions(
   187	  state: EncounterState,
   188	  actorId: CombatantId,
   189	  revision = state.revision,
   190	): EngineActorOptionPartition {
   191	  const subject = state.combatants.find((candidate) => candidate.profile.id === actorId);
   192	  if (subject?.profile.kind !== 'monster') return { offerable: [], humanOnly: [], candidates: [] };
   193	  const values = generateEngineOfferEnvelopes({ state, actorId, revision }).map(engineOfferableOption);
   194	  const offerable: EngineOfferableOption[] = [];
   195	  const humanOnly: EngineHumanOnlyOption[] = [
   196	    ...unsupportedActionCandidates(state, actorId, revision),
   197	    ...unsupportedBonusActionCandidates(state, actorId, revision),
   198	    ...unsupportedSpellCandidates(state, actorId, revision),
   199	  ];
   200	  for (const candidate of values) {
   201	    const modeling = classifyOptionModeling(state, {
   202	      kind: 'executable',
   203	      actorId: candidate.actorId,
   204	      movement: candidate.movement,
   205	      actionSlots: candidate.actionSlots,
   206	    });
   207	    if (modeling.kind === 'primary_effect_modeled') offerable.push(candidate);
   208	    else humanOnly.push(humanOnlyOption(
   209	      revision,
   210	      actorId,
   211	      candidate.label,
   212	      declaredIdentity(candidate),
   213	      modeling.reason,
   214	    ));
   215	  }
   216	  offerable.sort((left, right) => left.label.localeCompare(right.label) ||
   217	    left.optionId.localeCompare(right.optionId));
   218	  humanOnly.sort((left, right) => left.label.localeCompare(right.label) ||
   219	    left.optionId.localeCompare(right.optionId));
   220	  return { offerable, humanOnly, candidates: [...offerable, ...humanOnly] };
   221	}
   222	
   223	export function hiddenOptionRecords(
   224	  state: EncounterState,
   225	  actorIds: readonly CombatantId[],
   226	  revision: number,
   227	): readonly HiddenOptionRecord[] {
   228	  return [...new Set(actorIds)].sort((left, right) => left.localeCompare(right)).flatMap((actorId) =>
   229	    engineActorOptions(state, actorId, revision).humanOnly.map((option) => ({
   230	      actorId,
   231	      humanOptionId: option.optionId,
   232	      declaredOption: option.declaredOption,
   233	      reason: option.noModeledEffect,
   234	    })),
   235	  );
   236	}

   195	  const humanOnly: EngineHumanOnlyOption[] = [
   196	    ...unsupportedActionCandidates(state, actorId, revision),
   197	    ...unsupportedBonusActionCandidates(state, actorId, revision),
   198	    ...unsupportedSpellCandidates(state, actorId, revision),

   211	      candidate.label,
   212	      declaredIdentity(candidate),

   214	    ));

   219	    left.optionId.localeCompare(right.optionId));

   545	        const remaining = subject.limitedResources?.find((pool) =>

   607	export function generateStandardOfferDeclarations(

   632	        activationChoice: mainUse.activationChoice ?? bonusUse.activationChoice ?? null,

    98	function unlocatedTarget(
    99	  state: EncounterState,
   100	  observer: CombatantId,
   101	  targetId: CombatantId,
   102	): SuspectedTargetKnowledge | UnknownTargetKnowledge {
   103	  const observation = state.observationHistory.find((entry) =>
   104	    entry.observer === observer && entry.subject === targetId);
   105	  if (observation !== undefined) {
   106	    return {
   107	      kind: 'suspected',

   109	      lastSeen: {
   110	        status: 'resolved',

   112	      },
   113	    };
   114	  }
   115	  return {
   116	    kind: 'unknown',
   117	    targetId,
   118	    lastSeen: {
   119	      status: 'unresolved',
   120	      reason: 'never_observed',
   121	    },
   122	  };
   123	}

   125	function isPerceivedConditionName(name: ConditionName): name is PerceivedConditionName {
   126	  switch (name) {
   127	    case 'Blinded':
   128	    case 'Grappled':
   129	    case 'Paralyzed':
   130	    case 'Petrified':
   131	    case 'Prone':
   132	    case 'Restrained':
   133	    case 'Stunned':
   134	    case 'Unconscious': return true;
   135	    case 'Charmed':
   136	    case 'Deafened':
   137	    case 'Exhaustion':
   138	    case 'Frightened':
   139	    case 'Incapacitated':
   140	    case 'Invisible':
   141	    case 'Poisoned': return false;
   142	  }
   143	}

   154	    .sort((left, right) => left.condition.localeCompare(right.condition));
   155	}

   169	  };
   170	}

   172	function activeHitPoints(target: EncounterCombatantState): number {

   174	}

   176	function activeHitPointMaximum(

   226	export function projectActorKnowledge(

   270	          distanceFeet: minimumSpaceDistance(combatantSpace(state, actorId), space),

   303	  readonly costFeet: number;
   304	  readonly path: readonly GridCell[];

   307	
   308	function movementResolution(
   309	  state: EncounterState,
   310	  actorId: CombatantId,
   311	  movement: EngineMovementObjective,
   312	  slots: readonly EngineActionSlotUse[],
   313	  queries: EngineQueryPort,
   314	): MovementResolution | null {
   315	  const origin = queries.tokenPosition(state, actorId);
   316	  const actor = queries.combatant(state, actorId);
   317	  const constraints = targetConstraints(state, actorId, slots, queries);
   318	  if (origin === null || actor === null || constraints === null) return null;
   319	  const anchor = movement.engagement.anchor;
   320	  const productiveClose = constraints.length === 0 &&
   321	    movement.engagement.stance === 'close_to_melee' && anchor !== undefined && anchor !== null;
   322	  if (!productiveClose && positionFits(state, actorId, origin, constraints, movement, queries)) {
   323	    return { costFeet: 0, path: [], finalPosition: origin };
   324	  }
   325	  if (movement.preference.willingness === 'none') return null;
   326	  const maximumFeet = movement.preference.maximumFeet ?? actor.profile.rules.speed;
   327	  const movementKind = slots.some((slot) => slot.slot === 'main' && slot.use.kind === 'dash') ? 'dash' : 'normal';
   328	  if (productiveClose) {
   329	    const anchorId = resolveSelector(state, actorId, anchor, queries);
   330	    if (anchorId === null || queries.tokenPosition(state, anchorId) === null) return null;
   331	    const anchorPosition = minimumSpaceLine(
   332	      combatantSpace(state, actorId),
   333	      combatantSpace(state, anchorId),
   334	    ).targetCell;
   335	    const approach = queries.approach(state, {
   336	      actorId,
   337	      target: anchorPosition,
   338	      movement: movementKind,
   339	      maximumFeet,
   340	    });
   341	    if (!approach.legal) return null;
   342	    return {
   343	      costFeet: approach.costFeet,
   344	      path: approach.cells,
   345	      finalPosition: approach.cells.at(-1) ?? origin,
   346	    };
   347	  }
   348	  const candidateCells: { readonly lowerBoundFeet: number; readonly finalPosition: GridCell }[] = [];
   349	  for (let row = 0; row < state.bounds.rows; row += 1) {
   350	    for (let column = 0; column < state.bounds.columns; column += 1) {
   351	      const finalPosition = { column, row };
   352	      if (!positionFits(state, actorId, finalPosition, constraints, movement, queries)) continue;
   353	      const lowerBoundFeet = gridDistance(origin, finalPosition);
   354	      if (lowerBoundFeet <= maximumFeet) candidateCells.push({ lowerBoundFeet, finalPosition });
   355	    }
   356	  }
   357	  candidateCells.sort((left, right) => left.lowerBoundFeet - right.lowerBoundFeet ||
   358	    left.finalPosition.row - right.finalPosition.row || left.finalPosition.column - right.finalPosition.column);
   359	  let best: { readonly costFeet: number; readonly path: readonly GridCell[]; readonly finalPosition: GridCell } | null = null;
   360	  for (const candidate of candidateCells) {
   361	    if (best !== null && candidate.lowerBoundFeet > best.costFeet) break;
   362	    const result = queries.path(state, {
   363	      actorId,
   364	      destination: candidate.finalPosition,
   365	      movement: movementKind,
   366	      maximumFeet,
   367	    });
   368	    if (!result.legal) continue;
   369	    const resolved = { costFeet: result.costFeet, path: result.cells, finalPosition: candidate.finalPosition };
   370	    if (best === null || resolved.costFeet < best.costFeet ||
   371	      resolved.costFeet === best.costFeet && (resolved.finalPosition.row < best.finalPosition.row ||
   372	        resolved.finalPosition.row === best.finalPosition.row && resolved.finalPosition.column < best.finalPosition.column)) {
   373	      best = resolved;

codex
The first key distinction is now clear: raw declarations always include Dash, but the presented/usable set is filtered by resolution. Dash carries a `nearest_visible_enemy` anchor; resolution rejects it when that selector returns `null`. I’m checking the decision constraints and test pins next, including whether “detected” here means `seen` only or also nonvisual `located` (the code currently uses `seen` for that selector).

.claude/decisions.md:22418:The quiet-window scripts used two different mechanisms at once: an exit-file dependency AND a `pgrep -f "[v]erify-.*\.sh"` busy check. verify-offers-s3b.sh was queued behind gate-heldout.exit and, while merely sleeping in that wait loop, matched the busy pattern used by gate-quietstone-quiet.sh — which the heldout gate waits on. Circular: quietstone ← offers-waiter ← heldout ← quietstone. Load sat at ~0.9 with nothing running from 12:05 to 16:58 and no gate fired; the three gate monitors reported "waiting" correctly and the supervisor read that as a busy machine rather than checking the condition. Fix: killed the five waiters by PID and relaunched them as a strict linear chain with no pgrep condition — quietstone → heldout → d569b → offers 3B verify → handoff battery, each waiting only on its predecessor's exit file, with the real exit code recorded instead of a hardcoded 0. Quietstone gate started 16:58:39 at load 1.05. Rule: a queue may use exit-file ordering or a process-presence check, never both; a sleeping queued waiter is not a busy machine.

Each item keeps the D622 cadence: planned (sol) → plan reviewed (astra, ≤3 rounds) → implemented (sol) → reviewed (astra) → supervisor-gated before the next starts. .claude/decisions.md:22553:## D617.5 — OWNER (2026-09-14 14:13): offers — one environment builder module, imported by everyone
.claude/decisions.md:22555:Owner (verbatim): "there should only be one possible way to build the environment and then the round runner and the board projection and everything else need to import that env builder module." Binding design target for Slice 3's remainder: a single composition-root module is the only exported way to construct an EngineOptionEnvironment; the four constructors currently exported from src/vtt/offers/offer-environment.ts and called ad hoc from eight modules stop being reachable outside it; mode (legacy_standard / revision_bound) is a caller input to the one builder, never a second builder. Supervisor note: identity in the codebase is already by digest (capsule carries the binding digest; offered-option-paths raises OfferedOptionEnvironmentMismatchError), so the invariant is "one builder + digest equality", not object identity. The astra collaboration lane (D617.4) was stopped after ~5 minutes and restarted with this ruling in its brief (new session id in the loop-log).

.claude/decisions.md:22647:## D617.20 — SUPERVISOR (2026-09-15 09:29): plan defect — the frozen plan's gate wiring (:700, `test:gate = scripts/check-command-outcomes.sh && node tools/gate-vitest.mjs`, implemented in B1) violates M-3's executable gate inventory; bounded amendment ordered before B12
.claude/decisions.md:22648:Evidence (verified by me): tests/unit/vtt/handoff-report.test.ts fails 3/49 on the offers branch since B1 with `GATE_INVENTORY_INVALID: ARGV_NPM_TARGET_MISSING: unit-gate: node_modules/.bin/scripts/check-command-outcomes.sh`; passes 49/49 on main 75c2f44a; reproduced at 74192283 in a throwaway checkout. tools/vtt-handoff/gate-inventory.ts npmScriptTargets resolves each `&&` segment of an npm script as `node <file>` (file must exist) or `node_modules/.bin/<command>`; a repository shell script is neither. Neither the plan nor any batch list runs the M-3 suites, and B1's review accepted the wiring as matching §5. Amendment (binding, plan file untouched; manifest +1): add scripts/check-command-outcomes.mjs (node; runs the same four steps — sg scan src tools tests, sg test fixtures, architecture self-test, architecture scan — exiting non-zero on the first failure), make scripts/check-command-outcomes.sh delegate to it (one source), and set `test:gate = node scripts/check-command-outcomes.mjs && node tools/gate-vitest.mjs`. From now on every batch verification and the cumulative gate include tests/unit/vtt/handoff-report.test.ts and the other M-3 suites. B11 (db2a6ef8) is committed clean; the fix lands as a separate commit reviewed together with B11.

.claude/decisions.md:22672:Unit VIS-FIELD-01 opened (.claude/consensus/vis-field/): sol plans, astra reviews (≤3 rounds), sol implements, astra reviews, supervisor verifies and gates. Scope: (1) one pure engine function producing, per observer, the seen/dim/unseen state of every cell in bounds, reusing the existing tracer, light regions, obscurement regions/effects and senses; (2) its transpose (cells from which a creature can be seen); (3) fog derived from the party's fields (DM view) and the seat's owned fields (player view) — the authored foggedCells list is replaced, not accommodated; (4) the per-actor lists exported on the semantic payload as text; (5) heavily obscured and magical-darkness cells (fog cloud, darkness spell, obscurement regions) block sight THROUGH them along the traced line, not only at the target cell, unless the observer has a sense that defeats them (truesight; a new Devil's Sight sense for magical/nonmagical darkness within 120 ft per SRD; blindsight within range); (6) darkvision: darkness treated as dim and dim as bright within its range. SRD note recorded for the owner: RAW, dim light is visible to everyone (lightly obscured → Perception disadvantage); only darkness is unseeable without darkvision — the plan follows the SRD text in the repo and states that reading explicitly; a "dim needs darkvision" house rule is not adopted unless the owner says so after reading this note. No image, no model judge, no new art; hand-authored small-grid expectations; mutants per gate. SVG-fog Increment B: closed as a recorded deterministic rejection (option 1); QSFOG-SVG-01 closed; the Increment A repeatability numbers stand as the record of judge variance. D616's fog-contrast merge condition is superseded by this unit for the fog overlay (the overlay will render a derived set); the Quietstone merge (D616) is re-decided after VIS-FIELD-01 lands.

22672:Unit VIS-FIELD-01 opened (.claude/consensus/vis-field/): sol plans, astra reviews (≤3 rounds), sol implements, astra reviews, supervisor verifies and gates. Scope: (1) one pure engine function producing, per observer, the seen/dim/unseen state of every cell in bounds, reusing the existing tracer, light regions, obscurement regions/effects and senses; (2) its transpose (cells from which a creature can be seen); (3) fog derived from the party's fields (DM view) and the seat's owned fields (player view) — the authored foggedCells list is replaced, not accommodated; (4) the per-actor lists exported on the semantic payload as text; (5) heavily obscured and magical-darkness cells (fog cloud, darkness spell, obscurement regions) block sight THROUGH them along the traced line, not only at the target cell, unless the observer has a sense that defeats them (truesight; a new Devil's Sight sense for magical/nonmagical darkness within 120 ft per SRD; blindsight within range); (6) darkvision: darkness treated as dim and dim as bright within its range. SRD note recorded for the owner: RAW, dim light is visible to everyone (lightly obscured → Perception disadvantage); only darkness is unseeable without darkvision — the plan follows the SRD text in the repo and states that reading explicitly; a "dim needs darkvision" house rule is not adopted unless the owner says so after reading this note. No image, no model judge, no new art; hand-authored small-grid expectations; mutants per gate. SVG-fog Increment B: closed as a recorded deterministic rejection (option 1); QSFOG-SVG-01 closed; the Increment A repeatability numbers stand as the record of judge variance. D616's fog-contrast merge condition is superseded by this unit for the fog overlay (the overlay will render a derived set); the Quietstone merge (D616) is re-decided after VIS-FIELD-01 lands.

3732:PROPOSAL (to the owner, one question): adopt a SOLID-WALL model — the wall is the union of sight-blocking cells as closed rectilinear regions; a ray is blocked iff it passes through the union's interior, which includes (a) any blocking cell's interior, (b) an edge shared by two blockers (D635, already in), and (c) a vertex shared by two diagonally touching blockers (seal the crack; NOT in today). Grazing an OUTER face or a single blocker's corner stays open (DMG-consistent, today's behaviour).  16249	## D583 — engine blind spots and six candidate rooms where engine-top is not the best play (2026-09-08 08:14)
 16250	
 16251	Owner: "Assist Astra on trying to brainstorm rooms where the engine
 16252	recommendations are not optimal and there is a smarter play that the
 16253	engine doesn't see/rank higher". I supplied the actual ranking code so
 16254	the brainstorm ran against facts, not guesses. Full output:
 16255	.tmp/runs/astra-decision-06.log.
 16256	
 16257	THE RANKING, verbatim from src/vtt/intel/opportunity-cost.ts, sorted
 16258	ascending: [classRank, unresolvedFlag, -expected_damage_milli,
 16259	-attack_count, -approach_feet, resource_costs], where classRank is
 16260	offense 0, approach 1, dodge 2, everything else 3. Nothing in that tuple
 16261	references the target's REMAINING hit points, the opponent's next turn,
 16262	cover at the chosen endpoint, conditions inflicted, action-economy
 16263	denial, concentration, or coordination between two monsters.
 16264	
 16265	TWO CORRECTIONS ASTRA MADE TO MY OWN FRAMING, both from reading code I
 16266	had summarized too confidently:
 16267	- The default is chosen AFTER dominance filtering, not by the tuple
 16268	  alone (opportunity-cost.ts:267). A control option can eliminate an
 16269	  attack before the sort ever runs. So no room may be justified by the
 16270	  tuple; each needs a trace of the actual default.
 16271	- Spells are classified as OFFENSE, so a control spell does not
 16272	  automatically lose on classRank as I implied. It loses on unresolved
 16273	  status or on the damage field.
 16274	
 16275	BLIND SPOTS, in testing priority: (1) an attack that omits a useful
 16276	bonus-action heal, because adding Healing Word makes the evaluation
 16277	unresolved and the resolved attack wins on unresolvedFlag; (2) damaging
 16278	the easy target instead of incapacitating the dangerous one who acts
 16279	next, and overkill generally, since expected damage has no remaining-HP
 16280	term; (3) attacking instead of holding a chokepoint, since defence is
 16281	classRank 2 or 3; (4) preferring damage over a condition that denies a
 16282	turn; (5) no joint allocation across monsters; (6) -approach_feet
 16283	actually REWARDS walking farther for identical output.
 16284	
 16285	SIX CANDIDATE ROOMS designed, A through F. Astra would build three
 16286	first: A, attack plus Healing Word on a nearly-dead frontliner; B, an
 16287	Ogre javelin at the six-HP Fighter who acts next rather than the
 16288	healthier Wizard with better expected damage; C, an exposed advance
 16289	where the Greatclub gains damage but steps into two opponents' reach
 16290	when the javelin from cover is better. Estimated +1 to +4 panel points
 16291	each, subjective planning figures, not measurements.
 16292	
 16293	BUILDABILITY FINDINGS THAT MATTER: healing currently targets the first
 16294	living ally by id rather than offering every ally
 16295	(turn-option-registry.ts:411), so room A qualifies only if the offered
 16296	heal already targets the intended creature. Room E must use Ghast rather
 16297	than Ghoul because the offer builder suppresses standalone attacks when
 16298	a creature has multiattack. Room F needs a NEW capability, engine
 16299	authored split-target multiattack volleys, and the model must select a
 16300	complete engine-authored volley id rather than allocate attacks in
 16301	prose. None of these six is a product of existing seed flags; all need
 16302	authored snapshots with exact HP and initiative.
 16303	
 16304	THE FEASIBILITY CHECK Astra required before any nomination: a
 16305	mechanically verified WITNESS, with no judge involvement. Freeze room
 16306	and information boundary; capture the exact offers, dominance filtering
 16307	and actual default; prove the alternative is not merely selectable but
 16308	EXECUTABLE through the same acceptance and correction path the
 16309	experiment uses; compare consequences with live engine execution rather
 16310	than an imitation; follow through the threatened opponent turn and the
 16311	claimed allied follow-up against credible replies rather than a
 16312	cooperative opponent; and preregister materiality before searching
 16313	seeds. A single valid witness proves a better line exists; failure
 16314	proves only "not found under this search".
 16315	
 16316	THE TRAP, stated by Astra and accepted: hand-built rooms targeting known
 16317	defects demonstrate that this recommendation policy is exploitable on
 16318	deliberately selected cases, and if a model picks the certified
 16319	alternative, that it recognizes those cases. They do NOT establish that
 16320	models beat engine-top on ordinary rooms, that these failures are
 16321	common, that panel points predict encounter success, that the model
 16322	beats a REPAIRED heuristic, or that the earlier null was wrong. Verdict:
 16323	worth doing as a diagnostic challenge set, kept separate from the
 16324	ordinary room distribution, reported by flaw family, and with a simple
 16325	repaired heuristic as a comparator. Otherwise success may only mean the
 16326	model noticed a bug we deliberately placed in front of it.
 16327	
 16328	## D584 — a legacy invariance test has been RED SINCE INCREMENT 4 and everyone missed it (2026-09-08 08:17)
 16329	
 16330	The blind branch validation gate failed exactly one spec:
 16331	tests/unit/tools/ai-dm-legacy-invariance.test.ts, "keeps explicit
 16332	incumbent defaults byte-identical to the no-flag fixture".
 16333	`expect(record(implicit)).not.toHaveProperty('dmMode')` fails because
 16334	tools/ai-dm-conversation.ts:979 defaults dmMode to 'advice' and line
 16335	1103 always includes it. The spec's OTHER assertion, that the implicit
 16336	and fully explicit configs are deep-equal, PASSES.
 16337	
 16338	FINDING AGAINST OUR WHOLE VERIFICATION PRACTICE, mine included. I traced
 16339	five commits: the assertion and the field have coexisted since increment
 16340	4 (2167d6f2). So this test has been failing through increments 5 and 6,
 16341	the D578 amendments, the D579 corrections and the D576 integration.
 16342	Nobody saw it because every lane ran only its own "touched specs" list
 16343	and my harvest verification repeated those lists. The full gate is the
 16344	first thing that ever ran it. This is the identical gap I recorded when
 16345	the corner rule broke nine specs, and it recurred because I fixed the
 16346	symptom then rather than the rule.
 16347	
 16348	I did NOT cancel the gate this time, per Astra's ruling that cancelling
 16349	after a unit failure is not authorized standing policy. The browser
 16350	phase ran on.
 16351	
 16352	D584 RULINGS (Astra), all accepted:
 16353	
 16354	1. READING A, with a STRONGER test required. Keep the internal
 16355	   dmMode: 'advice' field. The approved plan defines the invariant as
 16356	   unchanged no-flag OUTPUTS (prompts, tools, rendering, image
 16357	   projection, persisted row shape), not as the absence of an internal
 16358	   config key, and it separately requires mode attribution for explicit
 16359	   D569 invocations. Astra also found a material gap in the EXISTING
 16360	   byte test: it reserializes the fixture's stored row instead of
 16361	   generating a row through the current runner, and its helper
 16362	   constructs the runtime directly, bypassing parsed-config threading.
 16363	   The replacement must therefore drive both configs through the
 16364	   production runner with a deterministic adapter, assert generated
 16365	   legacy rows and launcher manifests lack dmMode including recovery
 16366	   paths, compare protected protocol and row bytes against an
 16367	   independently established legacy oracle rather than against each
 16368	   other, control nondeterminism rather than stripping fields, and
 16369	   demonstrate that making attribution unconditional FAILS the new
 16370	   checks. Merely asserting 'advice', or equality, or successful
 16371	   fixture reserialization, is insufficient.
 16372	2. NO downstream contamination established, and none certified clean

 23052	## D641 — OWNER (2026-09-17 18:48): "I think we need to model that a wall is solid across cells. It is not just a series of cells. Look for how others have handled this." — research done by the supervisor; question put back to the owner
 23053	PROBED BY ME on 807d2e3c (traceTerrainLine, 6x6 board): (1) two blockers touching only at a corner, (2,1)&(1,2), observer (0,0) → target (3,3) through the shared vertex: tier half, blocksSight FALSE — the diagonal crack lets sight through; (2) solid 2x2 block: total, TRUE; (3) wall column with the ray along its face-line between two blockers (the D635 seam): half, TRUE; (4) a ray grazing one blocker's corner: none, FALSE. So today's tracer = closed cells whose interiors block + the D635 shared-EDGE rule; shared CORNERS of diagonally touching blockers are still open.
 23054	HOW OTHERS DO IT (sources in the reply): D&D 2014 DMG corner trace — lines from a corner to the target's corners; whether a line that merely TOUCHES an obstacle counts is explicitly the DM's call (the SRD 5.2.1 only defines cover degrees by "covers at least half / three-quarters / the whole target"); Gloomhaven — corner-to-corner lines, and "the line cannot touch or cross a wall at any point; touching the very edge of a wall still means no LOS" (walls are closed sets; touching = blocked); Foundry VTT / Roll20 — walls are SEGMENTS with endpoints (thin walls), not cells, so no cell seams exist and a long wall is one solid segment by construction; roguelikes (Red Blob "thin wall FOV", Adam Milazzo's survey, Albert Ford's symmetric shadowcasting, RogueBasin comparative study) — "thick walls" (blocking cells) vs "thin walls" (blocking edges) is the standard framing, and diagonal-gap peeking between corner-touching blockers is a known nuisance that implementations bevel or seal; Debenham & Solis-Oba, "New Algorithms for Computing Field of Vision over 2D Grids" (arXiv 2101.11002) — "adjacent vision blocking cells are first grouped together into rectilinear regions, then split into a minimal number of rectangles", and their Figure 5 is exactly our seam: two adjacent rectangles let a ray slip along the shared side, which they fix by extending one rectangle to overlap the other so the union is solid.
 23055	PROPOSAL (to the owner, one question): adopt a SOLID-WALL model — the wall is the union of sight-blocking cells as closed rectilinear regions; a ray is blocked iff it passes through the union's interior, which includes (a) any blocking cell's interior, (b) an edge shared by two blockers (D635, already in), and (c) a vertex shared by two diagonally touching blockers (seal the crack; NOT in today). Grazing an OUTER face or a single blocker's corner stays open (DMG-consistent, today's behaviour). Implementation: step 1 a local vertex rule beside firstSharedEdgeBlockingCell in cover.ts with witnesses for all four probe cases (small, rules-visible, needs its own D-ruling and astra review; lands with VIS-FIELD); step 2 the precomputed rectilinear-region/rectangle representation keyed by the blocking topology (the paper's approach) as the VIS-FIELD-PERF batch (also perf fix #3 in D635.53). Question 5 stays: regenerate the cohorts under the solid-wall geometry (A1).

   618	  return mechanics.actionSlots.every((slot) => targetedOffenseHasOpenTrace(state, mechanics, slot));

   652	    actorId: actor.id,
   653	  };
   654	}

   672	    }))),
   673	    actorId: actor.id,

   688

  1354	
  1355	Asked (round 2 Q11b): encounter-win probability with sequential

  1361	Consequences: the D461 ranking's objective is the probability of dropping
  1362	a character this round (team-scorer kill probability, computed under the
  1363	D476 knowledge ledger, so "confirmed" means confirmed from what the
  1364	monsters can observe and infer). Ties break on expected damage, then on
  1365	attack ETA for closing moves. Rankings are recomputed per actor in

  2154	/**
  2155	 * Refreshes only facts directly perceived in this state. An unperceived
  2156	 * subject's token is never read while retaining its earlier observation.
  2157	 */
  2158	export function reconcileObservationHistory(state: EncounterState): EncounterState {
  2159	  const hidden = new Set(state.hiddenCombatants.map((entry) => entry.combatant));
  2160	  const tokens = new Map(state.tokens.map((token) => [token.combatantId, token] as const));
  2161	  const presentCombatants = new Set(state.combatants.map((combatant) => combatant.profile.id));
  2162	  const presentLiving = new Set(state.combatants.flatMap((combatant) =>
  2163	    combatant.life !== 'dead' && tokens.has(combatant.profile.id)
  2164	      ? [combatant.profile.id]
  2165	      : []));
  2166	  const byPair = new Map(state.observationHistory
  2167	    .filter((entry) => presentCombatants.has(entry.observer) && presentLiving.has(entry.subject))
  2168	    .map((entry) => [observationKey(entry.observer, entry.subject), entry] as const));
  2169	  const validSpaces = new Map<CombatantId, ReturnType<typeof combatantSpace>>();
  2170	  for (const id of presentLiving) {
  2171	    try {
  2172	      validSpaces.set(id, combatantSpace(state, id));
  2173	    } catch (error) {
  2174	      if (!(error instanceof CreatureSizeRuleError)) throw error;
  2175	    }
  2176	  }
  2177	  const combatantIds = [...validSpaces.keys()].sort((left, right) => String(left).localeCompare(String(right)));
  2178	  for (const observer of combatantIds) {
  2179	    for (const subject of combatantIds) {
  2180	      if (observer === subject || hidden.has(subject) || !canCombatantSee(state, observer, subject)) continue;
  2181	      const token = tokens.get(subject);
  2182	      if (token === undefined) continue;
  2183	      const subjectSpace = validSpaces.get(subject);
  2184	      if (subjectSpace === undefined) continue;
  2185	      byPair.set(observationKey(observer, subject), {
  2186	        observer,
  2187	        subject,
  2188	        cell: { ...token.position },
  2189	        round: state.round,
  2190	        revision: state.revision,
  2191	      });
  2192	    }
  2193	  }
  2194	  return {
  2195	    ...state,
  2196	    observationHistory: [...byPair.values()].sort((left, right) =>
  2197	      String(left.observer).localeCompare(String(right.observer)) ||
  2198	      String(left.subject).localeCompare(String(right.subject))),
  2199	  };
  2200	}

 12853	export function reduceEncounter(
 12854	  state: EncounterState,
 12855	  command: EncounterCommand,
 12856	  rng: Rng,
 12857	  options: EncounterReductionOptions = {},
 12858	): EncounterReduction {

 12865	    reducerRng,
 12866	    rollOccurrenceId(`reducer/revision/${String(observedState.revision)}/command/${command.type}`),
 12867	  );
 12868	  const context: ReductionContext = {
 12869	    state: { ...observedState, revision: observedState.revision + 1 },
 12870	    rng: reducerRng,
 12871	    events: [],
 12872	    reactionDecision: options.reactionDecision ?? null,
 12873	  };
 12874	  const resolvedDecision = command.type === 'resolve_pending_decision'
 12875	    ? observedState.pendingDecisions.find((decision) => decision.id === command.decisionId)
 12876	    : undefined;
 12877	  const deferredLegendaryBoundary = resolvedDecision?.kind === 'legendary_action_window';
 12878	  const resumedLegendaryBoundary = command.type === 'end_turn' &&
 12879	    resumesLegendaryTurnBoundary(observedState, command.actor);
 12880	  processCommand(context, command);
 12881	  reconcileSearchMemories(context, visibilityBefore, command);
 12882	  advanceSearchMemories(context);
 12883	  const conclusion = deferredLegendaryBoundary
 12884	    ? null
 12885	    : encounterConclusionAfter(observedState, context.state) ??
 12886	      (resumedLegendaryBoundary
 12887	        ? encounterConclusionFromCurrentState(context.state)
 12888	        : null);
 12889	  if (conclusion !== null) context.state = { ...context.state, phase: conclusion };
 12890	  return {
 12891	    state: compactD420State(reconcileObservationHistory(context.state)),
 12892	    events: context.events,
 12893	  };
 12894	}

    61	/** Every serialized object carrying the exact grid coordinate, regardless of its field name. */
    62	function coordinatePaths(value: unknown, target: GridCell, path = '$'): string[] {
    63	  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') return [];
    64	  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    65	    return value.flatMap((entry, index) => coordinatePaths(entry, target, `${path}[${String(index)}]`));
    66	  }
    67	  const nested = Object.entries(value).flatMap(([key, entry]) =>
    68	    coordinatePaths(entry, target, `${path}.${key}`));
    69	  return 'column' in value && value.column === target.column &&
    70	    'row' in value && value.row === target.row
    71	    ? [path, ...nested]
    72	    : nested;
    73	}

   115	function valueAfter(arguments_: readonly string[], flag: string): string {
   116	  const index = arguments_.indexOf(flag);
   117	  const value = index < 0 ? undefined : arguments_[index + 1];
   118	  if (value === undefined || value.startsWith('--')) {
   119	    throw new Error(`Missing required ${flag} value.`);
   120	  }
   121	  return value;
   122	}
   123	
   124	export function parseInventoryArguments(
   125	  arguments_: readonly string[],
   126	): InventoryArguments {
   127	  return {
   128	    base: valueAfter(arguments_, '--base'),
   129	    baseline: valueAfter(arguments_, '--baseline'),
   130	    plan: valueAfter(arguments_, '--plan'),
   131	    out: valueAfter(arguments_, '--out'),
   132	    runtimeOut: valueAfter(arguments_, '--runtime-out'),
   133	  };
   134	}

   136	export function parsePlanManifest(plan: string): readonly string[] {
   137	  const start = plan.indexOf('## Slices and exact files');
   138	  const end = plan.indexOf('## D584.4 cumulative verification contract');
   139	  if (start < 0 || end <= start) {
   140	    throw new Error('Plan does not contain the bounded slices manifest.');
   141	  }
   142	  const manifest = plan.slice(start, end);
   143	  const paths = [...manifest.matchAll(/`((?:src|tests|tools)\/[^`]+)`/gu)]
   144	    .map((match) => match[1])
   145	    .filter((path): path is string => path !== undefined);
   146	  return [...new Set(paths)].sort();
   147	}
   148	
   149	export function parseBaseline(text: string): BaselineRecord {
   150	  let base: string | undefined;
   151	  let head: string | undefined;
   152	  let status: 'clean' | 'dirty' | undefined;
   153	  const paths: BaselinePath[] = [];
   154	  for (const line of text.split(/\r?\n/u)) {
   155	    if (line.length === 0 || line.startsWith('#')) continue;
   156	    const fields = line.split('\t');
   157	    if (fields[0] === 'base' && fields[1] !== undefined) base = fields[1];
   158	    else if (fields[0] === 'head' && fields[1] !== undefined) head = fields[1];
   159	    else if (fields[0] === 'status' && (fields[1] === 'clean' || fields[1] === 'dirty')) {
   160	      status = fields[1];
   161	    } else if (
   162	      fields[0] === 'path' &&
   163	      fields[1] !== undefined &&
   164	      fields[2] !== undefined &&
   165	      fields[3] !== undefined &&
   166	      fields[4] !== undefined
   167	    ) {
   168	      paths.push({
   169	        path: fields[1],
   170	        status: fields[2],
   171	        indexBlob: fields[3],
   172	        worktreeSha256: fields[4],
   173	      });
   174	    } else {
   175	      throw new Error(`Invalid baseline row: ${line}`);
   176	    }
   177	  }
   178	  if (base === undefined || head === undefined || status === undefined) {
   179	    throw new Error('Baseline must record base, head, and clean/dirty status.');
   180	  }
   181	  if ((status === 'clean') !== (paths.length === 0)) {
   182	    throw new Error('Baseline clean/dirty status disagrees with its path rows.');
   183	  }
   184	  return { base, head, status, paths };
   185	}
   186	
   187	export function parseNameStatus(text: string): readonly ChangeEntry[] {
   188	  return text.split(/\r?\n/u).flatMap((line) => {
   189	    if (line.length === 0) return [];
   190	    const fields = line.split('\t');
   191	    const status = fields[0];
   192	    const path = fields.at(-1);
   193	    if (status === undefined || path === undefined) {
   194	      throw new Error(`Invalid name-status row: ${line}`);
   195	    }
   196	    return [{ status, path }];
   197	  });
   198	}

   210	function matchesManifest(path: string, manifest: readonly string[]): boolean {
   211	  return manifest.some((entry) =>
   212	    entry.endsWith('/**') ? path.startsWith(entry.slice(0, -2)) : path === entry,
   213	  );
   214	}
   215	
   216	function scriptKind(path: string): ts.ScriptKind {
   217	  if (path.endsWith('.tsx')) return ts.ScriptKind.TSX;
   218	  if (path.endsWith('.js') || path.endsWith('.mjs')) return ts.ScriptKind.JS;
   219	  return ts.ScriptKind.TS;
   220	}
   221	
   222	function stringModuleSpecifier(node: ts.Expression | undefined): string | null {
   223	  return node !== undefined && ts.isStringLiteral(node) && node.text.startsWith('.')
   224	    ? node.text
   225	    : null;
   226	}

   228	/**
   229	 * Extracts only statically-known relative module edges from TypeScript syntax.
   230	 * Computed and template-literal dynamic imports are deliberately unsupported:
   231	 * they do not name one statically provable repository edge.
   232	 */
   233	export function extractRelativeImportSpecifiers(
   234	  path: string,
   235	  source: string,
   236	): readonly string[] {
   237	  const sourceFile = ts.createSourceFile(
   238	    path,
   239	    source,
   240	    ts.ScriptTarget.Latest,
   241	    true,
   242	    scriptKind(path),
   243	  );
   244	  const specifiers = new Set<string>();
   245	  const add = (value: string | null): void => {
   246	    if (value !== null) specifiers.add(value);
   247	  };
   248	  const visit = (node: ts.Node): void => {
   249	    if (ts.isImportDeclaration(node) || ts.isExportDeclaration(node)) {
   250	      add(stringModuleSpecifier(node.moduleSpecifier));
   251	    } else if (
   252	      ts.isImportEqualsDeclaration(node) &&
   253	      ts.isExternalModuleReference(node.moduleReference)
   254	    ) {
   255	      add(stringModuleSpecifier(node.moduleReference.expression));
   256	    } else if (ts.isImportTypeNode(node)) {
   257	      const argument = node.argument;
   258	      add(ts.isLiteralTypeNode(argument)
   259	        ? stringModuleSpecifier(argument.literal)
   260	        : null);
   261	    } else if (
   262	      ts.isCallExpression(node) &&
   263	      node.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ImportKeyword
   264	    ) {
   265	      add(stringModuleSpecifier(node.arguments[0]));
   266	    }
   267	    ts.forEachChild(node, visit);
   268	  };
   269	  visit(sourceFile);
   270	  return [...specifiers].sort();
   271	}
   272	
   273	function resolveRelativeImport(
   274	  consumer: string,
   275	  specifier: string,
   276	  files: ReadonlySet<string>,
   277	): string | null {
   278	  const raw = resolve(dirname(consumer), specifier);
   279	  const extension = extname(raw);
   280	  const bases = extension.length === 0
   281	    ? [raw, `${raw}.ts`, `${raw}.tsx`, `${raw}.mts`, `${raw}.mjs`, resolve(raw, 'index.ts')]
   282	    : [raw, extension === '.js' ? `${raw.slice(0, -3)}.ts` : raw];
   283	  return bases.find((candidate) => files.has(candidate)) ?? null;
   284	}
   285	
   286	export async function buildImportGraph(
   287	  root: string,
   288	  relativeFiles: readonly string[],
   289	): Promise<ImportGraph> {
   290	  const absoluteFiles = new Set(relativeFiles.map((path) => resolve(root, path)));
   291	  const imports = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
   292	  const consumers = new Map<string, Set<string>>();
   293	  await Promise.all([...absoluteFiles].map(async (consumer) => {
   294	    let source: string;
   295	    try {
   296	      source = await readFile(consumer, 'utf8');
   297	    } catch {
   298	      return;
   299	    }
   300	    for (const specifier of extractRelativeImportSpecifiers(consumer, source)) {
   301	      const producer = resolveRelativeImport(consumer, specifier, absoluteFiles);
   302	      if (producer === null) continue;
   303	      const consumerPath = relative(root, consumer);
   304	      const producerPath = relative(root, producer);
   305	      (imports.get(consumerPath) ?? (() => {
   306	        const values = new Set<string>();
   307	        imports.set(consumerPath, values);
   308	        return values;
   309	      })()).add(producerPath);
   310	      (consumers.get(producerPath) ?? (() => {
   311	        const values = new Set<string>();
   312	        consumers.set(producerPath, values);
   313	        return values;
   314	      })()).add(consumerPath);
   315	    }
   316	  }));
   317	  const sortedRecord = (values: ReadonlyMap<string, ReadonlySet<string>>) =>
   318	    Object.fromEntries([...values].sort(([left], [right]) => left.localeCompare(right))
   319	      .map(([key, entries]) => [key, [...entries].sort()]));
   320	  return {
   321	    importsByConsumer: sortedRecord(imports),
   322	    consumersByProducer: sortedRecord(consumers),
   323	  };
   324	}

   126	function requestedActors(capsule: EngineStateCapsule): readonly ProjectedActor[] {
   127	  if (capsule.request === null) return [];
   128	  const ids = new Set(capsule.request.actors);
   129	  return capsule.projection.combatants
   130	    .filter((actor) => ids.has(actor.id) && actor.life !== 'dead')
   131	    .sort((left, right) => left.id.localeCompare(right.id));
   132	}
   133	
   134	function explicitTargetIds(option: EngineOfferableOption): readonly CombatantId[] {
   135	  return option.actionSlots.flatMap((slot) => {
   136	    const use = slot.use;
   137	    switch (use.kind) {
   138	      case 'attack': return use.target.kind === 'combatant' ? [use.target.combatantId] : [];
   139	      case 'multiattack': return use.components.flatMap((component) =>
   140	        component.target.kind === 'combatant' ? [component.target.combatantId] : []);
   141	      case 'saving_throw': return use.target.kind === 'combatant' ? [use.target.combatantId] : [];
   142	      case 'cast_spell': return use.targets.flatMap((target) => target.kind === 'combatant' ? [target.combatantId] : []);
   143	      case 'use_world_object':
   144	      case 'dodge':
   145	      case 'disengage':
   146	      case 'dash':
   147	      case 'hide':
   148	      case 'end_turn': return [];
   149	    }
   150	  });
   151	}
   152	
   153	function isDefense(option: EngineOfferableOption): boolean {
   154	  return option.actionSlots.some((slot) => slot.slot === 'main' &&
   155	    (slot.use.kind === 'dodge' || slot.use.kind === 'end_turn'));
   156	}
   157	
   158	function isAdvance(option: EngineOfferableOption): boolean {
   159	  return option.actionSlots.some((slot) => slot.slot === 'main' && slot.use.kind === 'dash');
   160	}
   161	
   162	function isOffense(option: EngineOfferableOption): boolean {
   163	  return option.actionSlots.some((slot) => slot.slot === 'main' &&
   164	    (slot.use.kind === 'attack' || slot.use.kind === 'multiattack' || slot.use.kind === 'saving_throw'));
   165	}
   166	
   167	function isControl(option: EngineOfferableOption): boolean {
   168	  return option.actionSlots.some((slot) => {
   169	    const use = slot.use;
   170	    const ids = use.kind === 'multiattack'
   171	      ? [use.actionId, ...use.components.map((component) => component.actionId)]
   172	      : 'actionId' in use ? [use.actionId] : [];
   173	    return ids.some((id) => /web|grapple|grab/iu.test(id));
   174	  });

   177	function rankedTargets(capsule: EngineStateCapsule, actors: readonly ProjectedActor[]): readonly ProjectedActor[] {

   180	    .filter((actor) => actor.life !== 'dead' && actor.side !== side)
   181	    .sort((left, right) => left.hitPoints - right.hitPoints ||
   182	      right.reachFeet - left.reachFeet || left.id.localeCompare(right.id));
   183	}

   185	function chooseOption(
   186	  actor: ProjectedActor,
   187	  targets: readonly ProjectedActor[],
   188	  controlOnly: boolean,
   189	): EngineOfferableOption | null {
   190	  const targetRank = new Map(targets.map((target, index) => [target.id, index] as const));
   191	  const candidates = actor.options.filter((option) => controlOnly ? isControl(option) : isOffense(option));
   192	  candidates.sort((left, right) => {
   193	    const leftRank = Math.min(...explicitTargetIds(left).map((id) => targetRank.get(id) ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER));
   194	    const rightRank = Math.min(...explicitTargetIds(right).map((id) => targetRank.get(id) ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER));
   195	    const leftUses = left.actionSlots.reduce((count, slot) =>
   196	      count + (slot.use.kind === 'multiattack' ? slot.use.components.length : 1), 0);
   197	    const rightUses = right.actionSlots.reduce((count, slot) =>
   198	      count + (slot.use.kind === 'multiattack' ? slot.use.components.length : 1), 0);
   199	    return leftRank - rightRank || rightUses - leftUses || left.label.localeCompare(right.label);
   200	  });
   201	  return candidates[0] ?? actor.options.find(isAdvance) ?? actor.options.find(isDefense) ?? null;
   202	}

   204	function alternateOffense(
   205	  actor: ProjectedActor,
   206	  primary: EngineOfferableOption,
   207	  targets: readonly ProjectedActor[],
   208	): EngineOfferableOption | null {
   209	  const primaryTargets = new Set(explicitTargetIds(primary));

   213	      option.revision === primary.revision &&
   214	      explicitTargetIds(option).some((targetId) => !primaryTargets.has(targetId)))
   215	    .sort((left, right) => {
   216	      const leftRank = Math.min(...explicitTargetIds(left).map((id) => targetRank.get(id) ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER));
   217	      const rightRank = Math.min(...explicitTargetIds(right).map((id) => targetRank.get(id) ?? Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER));
   218	      return leftRank - rightRank || left.label.localeCompare(right.label);
   219	    })[0] ?? null;
   220	}

   339	function shadowIssues(

   360	    if (proposal.fallbackOptionId === proposal.primaryOptionId) issues.push('FALLBACK_EQUALS_PRIMARY');
   361	    if (proposal.fallbackOptionId !== null) {
   362	      const fallback = actor.options.find((option) => option.optionId === proposal.fallbackOptionId);
   363	      if (fallback === undefined) issues.push('FALLBACK_OPTION_NOT_PROJECTED');
   364	      else if (fallback.revision !== proposal.expectedRevision) issues.push('FALLBACK_REVISION_MISMATCH');
   365	    }
   366	  }
   367	  for (const actor of actors) {
   368	    if (!proposed.has(actor.id)) issues.push('MISSING_ACTOR');
   369	  }
   370	  return Object.freeze([...new Set(issues)]);
   371	}

   412	      playNames: ['remove_obstacle'],

   418	    skillDefinition(dependencies, plays, {
   419	      name: 'focus_fire',

   421	      procedure: 'Use focus_fire when removing one vulnerable opponent improves the team position. Preserve each complete engine option and its alternate-target fallback. Edit or discard the draft when objectives, morale, or resource conservation outweigh concentration.',
   422	      playNames: ['focus_fire'],

   424	      alwaysOn: false,
   425	      trigger: 'focus_fire is applicable',
   426	      applicability: (capsule) => playApplicable('focus_fire', capsule),
   427	    }),
   428	  ] satisfies readonly SkillDefinition[]);
   429	  const snippetHash = dependencies.hash(JSON.stringify({

   431	  }));
   432	  const snippetSetHash = dependencies.hash(JSON.stringify({
   433	    exposure: 'play', enabled: plays.map((play) => `${play.name}:${play.snippetHash}`).sort(),

   435	  const skillHash = dependencies.hash(JSON.stringify({

    51	        ? { stance: 'hold_position' }

    55	      ? [{ slot: 'main', use: { kind: 'dodge' } }]
    56	      : [{
    57	          slot: 'main',
    58	          use: action === 'attack'

     6	function withChoicePools(state: EncounterState): EncounterState {
     7	  return {
     8	    ...state,
     9	    combatants: state.combatants.map((combatant) => {
    10	      if (combatant.profile.kind !== 'monster') return combatant;
    11	      const existing = combatant.limitedResources ?? [];
    12	      const additions = declaredMonsterBonusActions(state, combatant.profile.id).flatMap((action) => {
    13	        if (action.kind !== 'spell_choice') return [];
    14	        return action.spells.flatMap((spell) => {
    15	          const id = monsterSpellResourcePoolId(action.id, spell);
    16	          const maximum = monsterSpellMaximumUses(spell);
    17	          return id === null || maximum === null || existing.some((pool) => pool.id === id)
    18	            ? []
    19	            : [{ id, maximum, remaining: maximum, recharge: 'long_rest' as const }];
    20	        });
    21	      });
    22	      const uniqueAdditions = [...new Map(additions.map((pool) => [pool.id, pool] as const)).values()];
    23	      return uniqueAdditions.length === 0
    24	        ? combatant
    25	        : { ...combatant, limitedResources: [...existing, ...uniqueAdditions] };
    26	    }),
    27	  };
    28	}

    39	        (preserveActiveActor && combatant.profile.id === state.activeCombatant)

  1060	function path(state: EncounterState, request: EnginePathRequest): EnginePathResult {

  1062	  const start = state.tokens.find((token) => token.combatantId === request.actorId)?.position;
  1063	  if (actor === undefined || start === undefined) return { legal: false, code: 'actor_not_placed' };
  1064	  const ordinaryBudget = state.activeCombatant === request.actorId
  1065	    ? actor.turn.movement.remaining
  1066	    : actor.profile.rules.speed;
  1067	  const availableBudget = request.maximumFeet ?? (
  1068	    request.movement === 'dash'
  1069	      ? ordinaryBudget + actor.profile.rules.speed
  1070	      : ordinaryBudget
  1071	  );

  1073	    ? availableBudget
  1074	    : Math.min(availableBudget, maximumPathCost(state));

  1076	    actorId: request.actorId,
  1077	    start,
  1078	    goal: request.destination,
  1079	    maximumCost: feet(searchBudget),
  1080	  });
  1081	  if (result.kind === 'found') {
  1082	    return {
  1083	      legal: true,
  1084	      cells: result.cells,
  1085	      costFeet: result.cost,
  1086	      budgetFeet: availableBudget,
  1087	    };
  1088	  }
  1089	  if (request.maximumFeet !== undefined && request.maximumFeet < maximumPathCost(state)) {
  1090	    const unbounded = findPath(encounterMovementWorld(state), {

  1092	      start,

  1094	      maximumCost: feet(maximumPathCost(state)),

  1098	  return { legal: false, code: 'destination_unreachable' };

The knowledge side already contains a usable last-seen primitive: `EncounterState.observationHistory` stores observer/subject/cell/round/revision and `projectActorKnowledge` exposes it as `suspected`; a never-observed PC is explicitly `unknown/never_observed`. The missing seam is not storage—it is offer targeting/resolution, which currently ignores `suspected` targets for Dash. I’m now measuring the affected population across the four frozen ten-room cohorts plus 6209 and separating “no current detection” from “can move anywhere legally.”

   286	function cellIsInBounds(
   287	  cell: { readonly column: number; readonly row: number },
   288	  bounds: { readonly columns: number; readonly rows: number },
   289	): boolean {
   290	  return cell.column >= 0 && cell.column < bounds.columns &&
   291	    cell.row >= 0 && cell.row < bounds.rows;
   292	}

   294	function assertBrutalMembership(
   295	  room: GeneratedRoom,

   305	  expect(room.spec.challengeSpentEighths, `seed ${String(seed)} minimum spend`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(

   307	  );
   308	  expect(room.spec.challengeSpentEighths, `seed ${String(seed)} maximum spend`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
   309	    room.spec.challengeBudgetEighths * BRUTAL_CHALLENGE_SPEND_FRACTION_BAND.maximum,
   310	  );
   311	
   312	  const roster = room.spec.monsterRoster.map((entry) => {
   313	    const row = BUNDLED_MONSTER_ROSTER.find((candidate) => candidate.id === entry.statblockId);

   320	      action.kind === 'spellcasting' && action.execution?.kind !== 'absent' &&
   321	      action.spells.some((spell) => spell.manifestStatus === 'implemented'));
   322	  }), `seed ${String(seed)} executable caster`).toBe(true);
   323	
   324	  const terrainCounts = {

   334	  expect(room.spec.terrain.length, `seed ${String(seed)} terrain exceeds hard`).toBeGreaterThan(

   336	  );
   337	  expect(room.spec.terrain.length, `seed ${String(seed)} terrain minimum`).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(
   338	    BRUTAL_TERRAIN_FEATURE_COUNT_BAND.minimum,
   339	  );
   340	  expect(room.spec.terrain.length, `seed ${String(seed)} terrain maximum`).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
   341	    BRUTAL_TERRAIN_FEATURE_COUNT_BAND.maximum,
   342	  );
   343	
   344	  const state = decodeArenaFixture(room);

   347	    ...state.environment.lightRegions,

    61	export function inventoryDigest(paths: readonly string[]): string {
    62	  return createHash('sha256').update(`${paths.join('\n')}\n`).digest('hex');

    65	export function healingPotionUsesComponentIngress(): boolean {
    66	  const encounter = readFileSync(resolve(ROOT, 'src/combat/encounter.ts'), 'utf8');
    67	  const start = encounter.indexOf("case 'drink_healing_potion'");
    68	  const end = encounter.indexOf('\n    case ', start + 1);
    69	  if (start < 0 || end <= start) return false;
    70	  const branch = encounter.slice(start, end);
    71	  return branch.includes('const healing = rollDice(context.rng') && !branch.includes('healing += rollDie(');
    72	}

    74	export function reverseConsumerClosure(
    75	  seeds: readonly string[],
    76	  reverse: ReadonlyMap<string, ReadonlySet<string>>,
    77	): ReadonlySet<string> {
    78	  const queue = [...seeds];
    79	  const visited = new Set(queue);
    80	  const consumers = new Set<string>();
    81	  while (queue.length > 0) {
    82	    const dependency = queue.shift();
    83	    if (dependency === undefined) break;
    84	    for (const consumer of reverse.get(dependency) ?? []) {
    85	      if (consumer.startsWith('tests/') && consumer.endsWith('.test.ts')) consumers.add(consumer);
    86	      if (!visited.has(consumer)) {
    87	        visited.add(consumer);
    88	        queue.push(consumer);
    89	      }
    90	    }
    91	  }
    92	  return consumers;
    93	}

   111	export interface DependencySpecifier {
   112	  readonly specifier: string;
   113	  readonly typeOnly: boolean;
   114	  readonly syntax: 'import' | 'export' | 'import_equals' | 'dynamic_import' | 'require' | 'import_type';
   115	}
   116	
   117	export function dependencySpecifiers(sourceText: string, fileName: string): readonly DependencySpecifier[] {
   118	  const source = ts.createSourceFile(fileName, sourceText, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, true, ts.ScriptKind.TS);
   119	  const result: DependencySpecifier[] = [];
   120	  const add = (specifier: string, typeOnly: boolean, syntax: DependencySpecifier['syntax']): void => {
   121	    result.push({ specifier, typeOnly, syntax });
   122	  };
   123	  const visit = (node: ts.Node): void => {
   124	    if (ts.isImportDeclaration(node) && ts.isStringLiteral(node.moduleSpecifier)) {
   125	      add(node.moduleSpecifier.text, node.importClause?.isTypeOnly === true, 'import');
   126	    } else if (ts.isExportDeclaration(node) && node.moduleSpecifier !== undefined && ts.isStringLiteral(node.moduleSpecifier)) {
   127	      add(node.moduleSpecifier.text, node.isTypeOnly, 'export');
   128	    } else if (ts.isImportEqualsDeclaration(node)) {
   129	      if (!ts.isExternalModuleReference(node.moduleReference) || node.moduleReference.expression === undefined ||
   130	        !ts.isStringLiteral(node.moduleReference.expression)) {
   131	        throw new Error(`Rejected unresolved TypeScript import-equals declaration in ${fileName}.`);
   132	      }
   133	      const specifier = node.moduleReference.expression.text;
   134	      if (!specifier.startsWith('.')) {
   135	        throw new Error(`Rejected external TypeScript import-equals declaration ${specifier} in ${fileName}.`);
   136	      }
   137	      add(specifier, node.isTypeOnly, 'import_equals');
   138	    } else if (ts.isImportTypeNode(node) && ts.isLiteralTypeNode(node.argument) && ts.isStringLiteral(node.argument.literal)) {
   139	      add(node.argument.literal.text, true, 'import_type');
   140	    } else if (ts.isCallExpression(node) && node.arguments.length === 1) {
   141	      const argument = node.arguments[0];
   142	      if (argument !== undefined && ts.isStringLiteral(argument)) {
   143	        if (node.expression.kind === ts.SyntaxKind.ImportKeyword) add(argument.text, false, 'dynamic_import');
   144	        if (ts.isIdentifier(node.expression) && node.expression.text === 'require') add(argument.text, false, 'require');
   145	      }
   146	    }
   147	    ts.forEachChild(node, visit);
   148	  };
   149	  visit(source);
   150	  return result;
   151	}
   152	
   153	function sourceFiles(directory: string): readonly string[] {
   154	  const result: string[] = [];
   155	  const visit = (current: string): void => {
   156	    for (const name of readdirSync(current)) {
   157	      if (name === 'node_modules' || name === '.git' || name.startsWith('.tmp')) continue;
   158	      const path = resolve(current, name);
   159	      const info = statSync(path);
   160	      if (info.isDirectory()) visit(path);
   161	      else if (['.ts', '.tsx', '.mts', '.cts'].includes(extname(path))) result.push(relative(ROOT, path));
   162	    }
   163	  };
   164	  visit(directory);
   165	  return result.sort();
   166	}
   167	
   168	export function resolveLocal(importer: string, specifier: string): string | null {
   169	  if (!specifier.startsWith('.')) return null;
   170	  const pathSpecifier = specifier.split('?')[0];
   171	  if (pathSpecifier === undefined) return null;
   172	  const base = resolve(ROOT, dirname(importer), pathSpecifier);
   173	  for (const candidate of [
   174	    base,
   175	    `${base}.ts`,
   176	    `${base}.tsx`,
   177	    `${base}.d.ts`,
   178	    `${base}.mts`,
   179	    `${base}.cts`,
   180	    resolve(base, 'index.ts'),
   181	    resolve(base, 'index.d.ts'),
   182	  ]) {
   183	    if (existsSync(candidate) && statSync(candidate).isFile()) {
   184	      return ['.ts', '.tsx', '.mts', '.cts'].includes(extname(candidate)) ? relative(ROOT, candidate) : null;
   185	    }
   186	  }
   187	  throw new Error(`Unresolved relative dependency ${specifier} from ${importer}.`);
   188	}
   189	
   190	export type GitRunner = (args: readonly string[]) => string | null;
   191	
   192	// Injected runners propagate exceptions; only this default adapter converts Git execution failures to null.
   193	export function gitOutput(args: readonly string[]): string | null {
   194	  try {
   195	    return execFileSync('git', args, {
   196	      cwd: ROOT,
   197	      encoding: 'utf8',
   198	      stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
   199	    });
   200	  } catch (_error: unknown) {
   201	    return null;
   202	  }
   203	}
   204	
   205	function changedPaths(git: GitRunner): readonly string[] {
   206	  const mergedMain = git(['merge-base', 'HEAD', 'main'])?.trim() ?? '';
   207	  const committed = git(['diff', '--name-only', 'main', '--']) ?? '';
   208	  const branchCommitted = new Set((mergedMain === ''
   209	    ? ''
   210	    : git(['diff', '--name-only', mergedMain, '--']) ?? '')
   211	    .split('\n').filter((path) => path.length > 0));
   212	  const untracked = git(['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard']) ?? '';
   213	  const changed = [...new Set(`${committed}\n${untracked}`.split('\n').filter((path) => path.length > 0))].sort();
   214	  for (const path of changed) {
   215	    if (path.startsWith('tests/') && path.endsWith('.test.ts') &&
   216	      !existsSync(resolve(ROOT, path)) && branchCommitted.has(path)) {
   217	      throw new Error(`D583 changed spec was deleted: ${path}`);
   218	    }
   219	  }
   220	  return changed.filter((path) => existsSync(resolve(ROOT, path)));
   221	}

   235	  }

   238	  }

   240	    inventoryDigest(TRIAL_CORE_RECONCILIATION_BASELINE_SPECS) !== TRIAL_CORE_RECONCILIATION_BASELINE_SHA256) {

   175	    `${base}.ts`,
   176	    `${base}.tsx`,
   177	    `${base}.d.ts`,
   178	    `${base}.mts`,
   179	    `${base}.cts`,
   180	    resolve(base, 'index.ts'),
   181	    resolve(base, 'index.d.ts'),
   182	  ]) {
   183	    if (existsSync(candidate) && statSync(candidate).isFile()) {

    61	function targetedOffenseHasOpenTrace(
    62	  state: EncounterState,
    63	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
    64	  slot: ResolvedActionSlotUse,
    65	): boolean {
    66	  if (slot.kind !== 'attack' && slot.kind !== 'saving_throw' && slot.kind !== 'cast_spell') {
    67	    return true;
    68	  }
    69	  return slot.targetIds.every((targetId) => {
    70	    const trace = traceCombatantLine(state, mechanics.actorId, targetId, {
    71	      sourceAnchor: mechanics.finalPosition,
    72	    });
    73	    return !trace.blocksSight && trace.tier !== 'total';
    74	  });
    75	}

    77	function resolvedMechanicsIsProductive(
    78	  state: EncounterState,
    79	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
    80	): boolean {
    81	  const hasProductiveComponent = mechanics.movementCostFeet > 0 ||
    82	    mechanics.actionSlots.some((slot) =>
    83	      slot.kind === 'attack' || slot.kind === 'saving_throw' || slot.kind === 'cast_spell' ||
    84	      slot.kind === 'use_world_object');
    85	  if (!hasProductiveComponent) return false;
    86	
    87	  // D635/D642/D643: live cohorts additionally require every targeted offensive component
    88	  // to remain sight-clear and non-total at its resolved origin. room-generator.ts:1227's
    89	  // generated-room predicate is intentionally stricter: it requires no cover at all.
    90	  return mechanics.actionSlots.every((slot) => targetedOffenseHasOpenTrace(state, mechanics, slot));
    91	}

    96	    return resolution.valid && resolvedMechanicsIsProductive(state, resolution.mechanics);
    97	  });
    98	}

    61	function targetedOffenseHasOpenTrace(
    62	  state: EncounterState,
    63	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
    64	  slot: ResolvedActionSlotUse,
    65	): boolean {
    66	  if (slot.kind !== 'attack' && slot.kind !== 'saving_throw' && slot.kind !== 'cast_spell') {
    67	    return true;
    68	  }
    69	  return slot.targetIds.every((targetId) => {
    70	    const trace = traceCombatantLine(state, mechanics.actorId, targetId, {
    71	      sourceAnchor: mechanics.finalPosition,
    72	    });
    73	    return !trace.blocksSight && trace.tier !== 'total';
    74	  });
    75	}
    76	
    77	function resolvedMechanicsIsProductive(
    78	  state: EncounterState,
    79	  mechanics: ResolvedTurnMechanics,
    80	): boolean {
    81	  const hasProductiveComponent = mechanics.movementCostFeet > 0 ||
    82	    mechanics.actionSlots.some((slot) =>
    83	      slot.kind === 'attack' || slot.kind === 'saving_throw' || slot.kind === 'cast_spell' ||
    84	      slot.kind === 'use_world_object');
    85	  if (!hasProductiveComponent) return false;
    86	
    87	  // D635/D642/D643: live cohorts additionally require every targeted offensive component
    88	  // to remain sight-clear and non-total at its resolved origin. room-generator.ts:1227's
    89	  // generated-room predicate is intentionally stricter: it requires no cover at all.
    90	  return mechanics.actionSlots.every((slot) => targetedOffenseHasOpenTrace(state, mechanics, slot));
    91	}

    93	function monsterHasProductiveOption(state: EncounterState, actorId: CombatantId): boolean {
    94	  return availableEngineActorOptions(state, actorId, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT).some((option) => {
    95	    const resolution = resolveEngineActorOption(state, option, OFFER_ENVIRONMENT);
    96	    return resolution.valid && resolvedMechanicsIsProductive(state, resolution.mechanics);
    97	  });
    98	}

3718:MEASURED (sol, both trees' production hashes identical before/after; my own numbers agree: vane 3077 → 6585 ms): vane-tpk 3180 → 6820 ms (2.14×). NOT more detection queries (0.83×) but each sight query expanding into per-target-cell traces (visibility-field.ts:431): traceSpaces 95k → 348k (3.67×), traceCornerLine 124k → 536k (4.33×); 91.7% of cell traces are pairwise sightToCreature detection (~4.8 s inclusive), only 8.3% the derived field itself (~0.55 s). The field's weak caches (visibility-field.ts:104) are keyed by EncounterState identity, so immutable reducer revisions make nearly every request cold (206 projections over 205 distinct revisions; 140 traces each). los-cover productive-option 5472 → 6139 ms (+12%): the seam scan (firstSharedEdgeBlockingCell 4.17M calls, 380 ms) plus ~0.7 s more in traceCornerLine; also 33,953 of 46,650 reach traces (72.8%) were for candidates then refused by RANGE — geometry evaluated before the cheap range check. D630 pair 33.6 → 41.5 s: replay.ts:238 projects DM + every PC per replayed revision (derived fog 3,361 calls); the replay file rebuilds the scripted gate 15 times (13 default) at ~1.9 s each.
3720:CORRECTNESS: no field computed for ineligible observers (eligibleVisibilityObserverIds :525 excludes dead/unplaced/adjudication-pending/unconscious); per-cell tracing for large footprints is correctness-sensitive (a single representative ray would regress); the seam scan is required work. State-identity caching = design smell, not a defect. DISPOSITION: (1)+(3) go into TEST-PERF-01 (owner's ranks 6/8/9 still pending); (2)+(4) = a VIS-FIELD-PERF batch after landing, planned and reviewed like any batch; the 5 s budgets are NOT re-pinned meanwhile.

22418:The quiet-window scripts used two different mechanisms at once: an exit-file dependency AND a `pgrep -f "[v]erify-.*\.sh"` busy check. verify-offers-s3b.sh was queued behind gate-heldout.exit and, while merely sleeping in that wait loop, matched the busy pattern used by gate-quietstone-quiet.sh — which the heldout gate waits on. Circular: quietstone ← offers-waiter ← heldout ← quietstone. Load sat at ~0.9 with nothing running from 12:05 to 16:58 and no gate fired; the three gate monitors reported "waiting" correctly and the supervisor read that as a busy machine rather than checking the condition. Fix: killed the five waiters by PID and relaunched them as a strict linear chain with no pgrep condition — quietstone → heldout → d569b → offers 3B verify → handoff battery, each waiting only on its predecessor's exit file, with the real exit code recorded instead of a hardcoded 0. Quietstone gate started 16:58:39 at load 1.05. Rule: a queue may use exit-file ordering or a process-presence check, never both; a sleeping queued waiter is not a busy machine.
